# ARCH-5: Safety logic is judged by what it does when it is wrong

- A failsafe triggers when the vehicle loses something its current flight depends on, and what it then does is a separate, configurable decision.
- Improve an existing failsafe rather than adding an overlapping one, and never let one feature disable or bypass another's protection (rmackay9, [#34210](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/34210)).
- Anything that can disarm, land or change mode in flight is designed for the case where it fires wrongly as much as for the case where it is right: landing detector false positives disarm vehicles in flight (rmackay9, [#20929](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/20929)).

Confirmed 2026-10-14. Part of the root playbook, under [Architectural Principles](../claude/CLAUDE.md#architectural-principles). [All architectural rules](../README.md#architectural-rules)
